patient.name: Eleanor Whitfield
patient.chiefComplaint: Unresponsive, found by home health aide

history.hpi: Home health aide arrived for a scheduled visit and found the patient unresponsive in her recliner, empty coffee cup nearby. Aide reports the patient is a type 2 diabetic on insulin who ate poorly yesterday and skipped breakfast this morning. No witnessed seizure activity reported.
medications: Insulin lispro sliding scale with meals
history.lastOralIntake: Sips of water this morning per aide; no food since dinner last night
history.events: Home health aide found the patient unresponsive during a scheduled visit and called 911 immediately

scene.location: Single-story home, living room, patient found unresponsive in a recliner
scene.safety: No hazards noted; home health aide present and cooperative
scene.bystanders: Home health aide present, found the patient and called 911, able to provide medication history
visualCues: Patient slumped in recliner, eyes closed
Empty insulin pen and used test strips on side table
No vomitus or signs of trauma

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 79-year-old female unresponsive in a recliner. She does not respond to verbal stimuli and withdraws only to painful stimuli. A fingerstick glucose is obtained and reads 28 mg/dL.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent but at risk; occasional snoring respirations
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present but weak; skin diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Withdraws to painful stimuli only, no purposeful movement
otherFindings: No signs of trauma or seizure activity

expectedActions.shortAction: Confirm blood glucose 28 mg/dL by fingerstick before treatment
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms hypoglycemia and establishes a baseline before dextrose administration.

expectedActions.shortAction: Maintain airway positioning and monitor SpO2 given depressed mental status
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: With depressed mental status, initial focus is on airway protection, oxygenation, ventilation, and perfusion
expectedActions.rationale: Unresponsive patients are at risk for airway compromise independent of the glucose correction.

expectedActions.shortAction: Use D10% concentration preferentially over D50% given extravasation risk in fragile veins
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Dextrose 50% can cause local tissue damage if it extravasates from vein and may cause hyperglycemia. Dextrose 50% carries risk for little clinical gain. EMS systems may consider carrying no more than 25% concentration of dextrose for treating hypoglycemia in adults
expectedActions.rationale: Geriatric patients often have fragile, friable veins where D50% extravasation risk is elevated.

expectedActions.shortAction: Dextrose 10% IV in incremental doses, max 250 mL (25 g); reassess mental status after each dose
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Unconscious patient, or patients who are unable to protect their own airway: Dextrose IV – administer in incremental doses until mental status improves or maximum field dosing is reached (if available, D10% is preferred). Maximum field adult dosing: 25 g of 10–50% dextrose IV: 250 mL of 10% dextrose
expectedActions.rationale: Incremental dosing to a defined maximum avoids overshoot hyperglycemia while correcting hypoglycemia.

expectedActions.shortAction: Monitor IV site closely for infiltration throughout dextrose administration
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Dextrose 50% can cause local tissue damage if it extravasates from vein
expectedActions.rationale: Undetected infiltration wastes the dose and risks local tissue injury.

transitions.condition: Crew establishes IV access and administers incremental IV dextrose per protocol after confirming blood glucose 28 mg/dL and recognizing the patient as unresponsive and unable to protect her airway.
The IV site is not monitored during dextrose administration; infiltration occurs, halting the infusion before an adequate dose is delivered.

phases.name: IV dextrose given
phases.description: Crew establishes IV access, confirms hypoglycemia with fingerstick glucose 28 mg/dL, and administers incremental IV dextrose given the patient's inability to protect her airway. D10% is used preferentially over D50% given her fragile, geriatric veins.
phases.triggerCondition: After confirming blood glucose of 28 mg/dL and assessing the patient as unresponsive with inadequate airway protection, the crew establishes IV access and begins incremental IV dextrose administration per protocol, preferring the 10% concentration due to extravasation risk in a fragile geriatric patient.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent, occasional snoring; positioned to maintain patency
clinicalPresentation.circulation: IV access established in a fragile forearm vein; weak radial pulses
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Withdraws to painful stimuli only, no purposeful movement
otherFindings: IV dextrose 10% infusing in incremental doses

expectedActions.shortAction: Recheck blood glucose after dextrose; repeat dose if mental status remains abnormal
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Reassess vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, neurologic status assessment) and mental status. Repeat check of blood glucose level if previous hypoglycemia and mental status has not returned to normal
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms adequate correction and guides whether further dextrose is needed.

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport to appropriate facility given initial unresponsiveness requiring IV dextrose
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If hypoglycemia with continued symptoms, transport to closest appropriate receiving facility
expectedActions.rationale: A patient who required IV dextrose for unresponsive hypoglycemia warrants hospital evaluation despite improvement, particularly given CKD and insulin dosing risk.

transitions.condition: Incremental IV dextrose administration corrects the patient's glucose and mental status improves toward baseline.

phases.name: Mental status improved
phases.description: After incremental IV dextrose administration, the patient's mental status improves and she becomes alert and oriented to person and place. Repeat glucose is checked and she is prepared for transport given her diabetes and initial unresponsiveness.
phases.triggerCondition: After incremental IV dextrose administration, the patient's mental status improves and she becomes alert; repeat glucose is checked and she is packaged for transport per protocol given her initial unresponsiveness.

otherFindings: Oriented to person and place, mildly confused on time
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "What happened? I remember feeling shaky earlier and then nothing."

phases.name: IV site not monitored, infiltrates
phases.description: The IV site is not monitored during dextrose administration; the site swells and the infusion is recognized as infiltrated after an inadequate dose has been delivered. With IV access lost, the crew must switch to IM glucagon.
phases.triggerCondition: The IV site was not monitored during dextrose administration; infiltration occurs, causing local swelling and pain, and the infusion is stopped before an adequate dose is delivered. With IV access lost, the crew administers glucagon IM as an alternative treatment for continued hypoglycemia.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: IV site swollen, cool, and tender; infusion stopped
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Withdraws to painful stimuli only, no purposeful movement
otherFindings: Forearm swelling and pain at the IV site
Dextrose infusion stopped due to infiltration

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize IV infiltration; stop infusion and remove the IV
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Dextrose 50% can cause local tissue damage if it extravasates from vein
expectedActions.rationale: Continuing infusion into infiltrated tissue causes further local injury and delivers no therapeutic benefit.

expectedActions.shortAction: Glucagon 1 mg IM given after IV access failure
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Glucagon IM/IN – an option for patients for whom IV access cannot be established. Adult dosing: 1 mg IM/IN (or prefilled 3 mg dry powder IN or prefilled IM autoinjector)
expectedActions.rationale: Glucagon provides an alternative route to correct hypoglycemia when IV access is lost.
